subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Peru's Nazca Lines were created between 500 BCE and 500 CE by the Nazca people.
• The geoglyphs have been studied by archaeologists since the early twentieth century.
• Ground-penetrating radar is an advanced geophysical technique that uses radio waves to detect subsurface structures.
• Archaeologist Dr. Soledad Tapia applied ground-penetrating radar to survey areas near the Nazca Lines.
• Tapia's analysis identified dozens of previously unknown geoglyphs beneath the desert surface.
prompt: The student wants to present Tapia's research to an audience unfamiliar with the Nazca Lines. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Using advanced geophysical techniques, Tapia identified dozens of previously unknown geoglyphs beneath Peru's Nazca Lines, ancient designs created by the Nazca people.
choices.B: Tapia surveyed areas near the Nazca Lines and then applied ground-penetrating radar to the data.
choices.C: Ground-penetrating radar is an advanced geophysical technique that Tapia used to detect subsurface structures.
choices.D: Created by the Nazca people between 500 BCE and 500 CE, Peru's Nazca Lines concealed dozens of geoglyphs beneath the desert surface.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence effectively presents Tapia's research to an audience unfamiliar with the Nazca Lines, explaining the results of the research and identifying the Nazca Lines as ancient designs created by the Nazca people in Peru.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. While the sentence explains what the Nazca Lines are, it fails to present Tapia's research.
